newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage banks' profit margin 8.8 pct in '95 - MBA.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage banks' profit margin 8.8 pct in '95 - MBA.

text.p: On average, profit margins rose to 8.8 percent in 1995 from 4.6 percent in 1994 for firms involved in mortgage banking, according to a Mortgage Bankers' Association of America (MBA) survey of 309 companies.
Profit margin is net income divided by gross income.

"In 1995, mortgage companies were able to register a profit without having to rely so heavily on servicing sales as they did in the more difficult market of 1994," David Loreah, chief economist at MBA, said in a statement.
"While there are signs of progress, profit margins remain relatively narrow," Loreah added.
Firms that serviced between $1 billion and $3.99 billion were the most profitable group, with a profit margin of 16.7 percent, the study found.
